chunks.text: 28-year-old female, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Queenstown, Singapore.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim from the anesthesia team. Today, we'll discuss your upcoming laparoscopic cholecystectomy and the anesthesia plan. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready to talk.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. Can you tell me about your gallbladder issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've had pain in my tummy for months, especially after eating. The doctor said I have gallstones and need the surgery to remove the gallbladder.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're currently taking amlodipine for blood pressure, fluticasone nasal spray for allergies, and lisinopril was stopped recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, lah. I take amlodipine every morning, and the nasal spray twice daily. The doctor stopped lisinopril last week because of the surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, about allergies. Do you have any allergies to sulfa-containing medications or other antibiotics?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes! I had a bad rash from a sulfa antibiotic years ago. The doctor said it's a sulfa allergy, so I avoid all sulfa drugs now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Important to know. Any other allergies or reactions to medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just the sulfa. My nose gets itchy sometimes, but that's from pollen, not medications.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Got it. When did you last eat or drink anything?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had dinner at 7 PM last night and water until 10 PM. No food since then, as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Have you had anesthesia before? Any issues with previous surgeries?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first surgery. I'm a bit nervous, but I trust you all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We'll take good care of you. Finally, how are you managing daily activities? Any difficulty walking or climbing stairs?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk and do normal things, but sometimes my blood pressure is high. I take my meds regularly, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with general anesthesia and intubation as planned. You'll be asleep during the surgery and wake up in recovery. Any questions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] peripheral IV placed, 20 gauge

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] arterial line placed, radial artery

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] fluid bolus one hundred milliliters normal saline given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] blood pressure dropped to 80 over 50, treated with phenylephrine ten micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] heart rate increased to 110, treated with esmolol twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit sore, but okay lah. My tummy is achy, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you rate your pain on a scale from 0 to 10 for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 4? It’s manageable, but I can feel it when I move.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? Sometimes anesthesia can cause that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no vomiting. Just a bit of dizziness when I sat up earlier, but it went off.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How’s your breathing? Any tightness or discomfort in your chest or throat?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Throat’s a bit sore from the tube, but I can breathe fine. No wheezing or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything about the surgery itself? Sometimes patients have fuzzy memories.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, everything’s blank from when I went to sleep. Woke up here, so all good.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You have a history of hypertension and allergies. Any issues with those today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Blood pressure’s been fine, no headaches. Allergies? Nose is clear, no sneezing.
